variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables are assigned using a colon (:). Q is a wrapper over K, typically used in kdb+.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
int: 42i
float: 3.14f
char: "a"
str: "hello"
bool: 1b
sym: `hello
date: 2023.01.01
time: 12:00:00.000
data_types.notes: Q introduces distinct scalar types with suffixes (like i, f) and rich temporal types (date, time, timestamp).

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
sum: 3 + 4
diff: 10 - 5
prod: 2 * 3
quot: 10 % 2

eq: 1 = 1
neq: 1 <> 2
gt: 2 > 1
operators.notes: Evaluation is right-to-left. Division is %. Equality is = and inequality is <>.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: cond ($) is used for scalar conditions. The vector conditional (?) operates element-wise over arrays.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
/ Implicit looping via adverbs like each
squares: {x*x} each til 5

/ Explicit loop
x: 0
do[5; show x; x+:1]
for_loop.notes: til 5 generates 0..4. the 'each' adverb maps the function. 'do' provides an explicit count-based loop.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: The while loop continues until the condition becomes 0 or false.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions are defined in braces. x, y, and z are implicit parameters if not specified in the signature.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
vec: 1 2 3 4 5
mat: (1 2 3; 4 5 6)

firstElement: vec 0
count: count vec
arrays.notes: Lists are whitespace-separated. Indexing is zero-based, accessible via juxtaposition or square brackets.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
dict: `a`b`c ! 1 2 3
val: dict `b

keysDict: key dict
valsDict: value dict
maps.notes: Dictionaries use the ! operator (bang) between a list of keys and a list of values. Symbols (`) are commonly used as keys.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: The protected evaluation operator (@ or .) traps exceptions, passing the error string to a custom handler function.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: ReScript uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: ReScript supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: ReScript treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: ReScript performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: ReScript represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: ReScript formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in ReScript, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: ReScript constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code: for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x * x
iterators.notes: ReScript achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.code:
defmodule Person do
  defstruct [:name, :age]
  def greet(%Person{name: name}), do: "Hello #{name}"
end
oop_classes.notes: ReScript emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in ReScript are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: ReScript uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: ReScript provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
defmodule MyModule do
  import Enum, only: [map: 2]
  alias MyProject.Helper
end
modules_import.notes: ReScript isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
